_comment: A+ bank authoring fragment template. Write one file per domain: web/scripts/data/frags/aplus-1201-d1.json etc. Merge with: python3 web/scripts/merge-aplus-fragments.py 1201
_schema: mcqs: scenario-format multiple choice. single-choice = exactly 4 options, correctOptionIds = 1 id, selectCount = 1. multiple-choice ('Which TWO') = 5-6 options, correctOptionIds = 2 ids, selectCount = 2. IDs: a1-<domain>-<3-digit> (1201) / a2-<domain>-<3-digit> (1202), sequential from 001 within the domain. Every MCQ: format 'scenario', kind 'single-choice'|'multiple-choice', domain int, objective string, prompt (the QUESTION - scenario style, ends with a question), context (2-3 sentence scenario restatement), options (id 'a'-'f', text, rationale for EACH option incl. correct), correctOptionIds, selectCount, explanation (why correct + why distractors wrong), sourceRefs [{source: 'comptia', section: 'Objective X.Y'}, {source: 'professor-messer', section: '220-1201 <objective short name>'}]. ALL TEXT MUST BE ORIGINAL - never copy vendor question text. Fact-check numbers (ports, speeds, capacities) against the official objectives.

mcqs.prompt: A technician is provisioning a new server that will run four virtual machines for a small business. The technician installs a hypervisor directly on the server hardware, with no host operating system underneath. Which hypervisor type is being deployed?
mcqs.context: A new server runs four VMs; the hypervisor is installed directly on the hardware with no host OS underneath.

options.rationale: A Type 2 hypervisor runs as an application on top of a host operating system (e.g., VirtualBox, VMware Workstation).
A Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor installs directly on the hardware and manages VMs without a host OS — the deployment described.
Containers share the host kernel rather than virtualizing hardware; no hypervisor is involved.
Emulators translate instructions for a different CPU architecture; a native hypervisor virtualizes the same architecture.

mcqs.explanation: Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisors such as VMware ESXi, Microsoft Hyper-V, and Proxmox install directly on hardware and provide the VM management layer without a host OS. Type 2 hypervisors run inside a general-purpose OS.
